narrative.overview:
The game is played at a friend's fold-out table. The room is a dark walnut ground (a flat vertical gradient from walnut to deeper walnut, closed by a radial vignette), the playing surface is a teal felt topper shaped as a heavily rounded square with a dashed stitch seam and a fine noise nap, and the money is clay chips seen from above. Faces sit around the felt in seats sized from the room itself, so video dominates the frame rather than hiding in thumbnails.

One lamp lights the table. A soft warm pool of light slides to whoever must act while every other occupied seat dims; the same amber is the only saturated colour on any control, and it means exactly one thing: *you can do this now*. Everything else is bone on walnut or teal, quiet and legible at night.

Hierarchy is carried by scale, weight and position, never by colour or ornament. The pot and the amount to call are the largest things on screen; stacks, blinds and timers are set in a single workhorse sans with tabular numerals so numbers never jitter. Time is shown as exact-length bars, not rings or spinners.
keyCharacteristics: Walnut room, teal felt topper, clay chips, bone paper cards: four materials, nothing else.
One amber lamp, reserved for action, the acting seat, focus and the turn timer.
Scale-only hierarchy: pot and amount-to-call are huge, labels are small and muted.
One sans family (Figtree Variable, self-hosted), tabular numerals everywhere.
Container-sized seats (cq units) so faces dominate at any viewport.
Textures are inline SVG and CSS gradients only; no shipping rasters.

rules.name: The One Lamp Rule
rules.body: Amber appears only on something you can do now (enabled action buttons, the sit-down hover, toggles, slider thumb), on the seat that must act, on its turn timer, and on keyboard focus. Never on decoration, labels, headings or idle state. Lamp *light* (the low-alpha warm radial pool in the room, the faint warm wash at the top of the lobby) is atmosphere, not paint, and never forms a solid shape.

rules.name: The Chips Are Money Rule
rules.body: Clay-chip hues belong to chips. They are never used for UI states, categories or accents (the one exception is the blind clock turning chip-green during a break).

rules.name: The Dim Room Rule
rules.body: When someone must act, every other occupied seat drops to `brightness(0.7) saturate(0.85)` and the felt deepens one step to `felt-700`. Contrast moves toward the actor; nothing else is added.

rules.name: The Scale-Only Rule
rules.body: Importance is expressed by size and weight, not by colour, boxes or ornaments. The two biggest numbers on screen are the pot and what it costs you to stay in.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every number is set with tabular numerals so stacks, timers and blinds never shift width as they change.

rules.name: The Objects Cast Shadows Rule
rules.body: Only things that would cast a shadow on a real table (felt, cards, chips, button) or that float above it (sheets, toasts) get one. Bars, panels and seats stay flat.

dos: Do keep amber (`lamp`) to enabled actions, the acting seat, its turn timer and focus.
Do make the pot and the amount to call the largest type on screen (800 weight, tight negative tracking).
Do set every number with tabular numerals.
Do size seats from the room container (cq units) so faces dominate.
Do draw felt as a rounded square on a dark rail ring, with the noise nap and a 1.5px dashed stitch seam.
Do show time as exact-length bars that drain left to right.
Do use one clay colour per denomination, choosing the low or high set from the small blind.
Do build textures from inline SVG and CSS gradients; self-host the font.
donts: Don't put amber on decoration, headings, labels, tabs, idle states or chip denominations.
Don't add wood-grain texture to the walnut; the room is a flat gradient with a vignette.
Don't use chip colours for UI states or categories.
Don't use uppercase tracked labels; labels are sentence case at 12.5–13px.
Don't ship raster textures or remote font files.
